items.title: SAP confirms a cyberattack after reports hackers copied and altered source code
items.why: Hackers reportedly used stolen employee login tokens to reach SAP's GitHub and copy and change code. SAP says it has seen no access to customer business data and has rotated signing keys and limited GitHub access.
items.action: Ask your SAP partner whether any action is needed, and make sure developer tokens in your own GitHub or GitLab are short-lived and tied to multifactor sign-in.

items.title: Hackers breached Cloud One, one of the US Air Force's main cloud platforms
items.why: Reuters reports the intrusion was found about a month ago during an upgrade; one source says a software flaw gave access to the platform's control plane. Migrations are paused, updates are blocked, and data theft is not confirmed.
items.action: Lock down your cloud admin consoles: require multifactor sign-in for every admin, review who holds admin rights, and patch management tools as soon as fixes ship.

items.title: CISA adds 10 exploited flaws, led by Mitel MiCollab bugs used in data-theft attacks
items.why: Five Mitel MiCollab flaws were used as zero-days to plant web shells and steal data; flaws in Juniper Session Smart Router, Xen Orchestra and Danfoss store controllers were also added to CISA's exploited list.
items.action: Update Mitel MiCollab to 10.3.0.18 or later today; if you can't, block outside access to its AWV web conferencing component and check the server for unfamiliar files.

items.title: FinCEN takes some systems offline after an intrusion and extends filing deadlines
items.why: The Treasury's financial crimes agency confirmed unauthorized access to some systems. BSA E-Filing stays up, and some reports that were due Nov. 18, including beneficial ownership filings, are now due Dec. 30.
items.action: Check with your bookkeeper or compliance lead whether any FinCEN filing is affected by the new Dec. 30 deadline, and treat any email claiming to be from FinCEN with caution.

items.title: Colorado's myColorado app breach may expose ID photos of about 100,000 people
items.why: Attackers reached uploaded documents in the state app, including photos of driver's licenses, vehicle registrations and insurance cards. The app is offline, no payment data was taken, and notices began Nov. 27.
items.action: If you or staff use myColorado, watch for the state's notice, consider a credit freeze, and treat calls or emails citing your ID or insurance details with caution.

items.title: Unpatched Cacti flaw lets an attacker take over the server in four requests
items.why: Public exploit code shows how the guest account in Cacti 1.2.31, a network monitoring tool many IT teams run, can be used to run commands on the server. No fix or CVE exists yet, and no attacks have been reported.
items.action: Turn off the Cacti guest account, limit access to the Cacti web page to your internal network or VPN, and watch for the vendor's fix.
